passage:
Counsellor's note, Monday. Indu asked to see me privately. She had seen her close friend Payal send unkind messages about a new girl to a group chat. Indu felt torn: Payal is her friend, and she did not want to be the one who told. That afternoon, on the way to the bus, she spoke to Payal first. Payal called it a joke.
On Thursday Indu came back. The messages had continued and the new girl had stopped coming to lunch. Indu said, "Being loyal to Payal can't mean staying quiet about this." She gave me the dates and what she had seen.
I thanked her, then spoke with the new girl's family and with Payal separately, without naming Indu. I will follow up with both girls next week.
Mr. Bose

qa.q: Where did Indu speak to Payal?
qa.a: She spoke to Payal on the way to the bus.
Payal is her friend and she did not want to be the one who told, yet the messages were hurting the new girl.

qa.q: What order of steps worked for Indu, and what could she do if things continue?
qa.a: She talked to Payal first and, when the harm continued, told a trusted adult with dates; she could keep checking on the new girl.

qa.q: How might the new girl have experienced the messages?
qa.a: She stopped coming to lunch, which suggests she felt hurt and wanted to avoid other students.

grounding: A teen torn between loyalty and right talks to the friend first, then tells a trusted adult when the bullying continues.
